A lighthouse is a tower, building, or other structure designed to emit light from a system of lamps and lenses and to serve as a navigational aid for maritime pilots at sea or on inland waterways.

Most lighthouses emit a flashing regular pattern of light, which allows mariners to identify the specific lighthouse and distinguish it from other light sources.

Lighthouses are often located on coastlines, rocky outcrops, or islands to warn ships of dangerous areas and guide them safely through channels.
